How confidence is setIt follows the kind of evidence, not judgement.
  • The customer's own statement (high confidence at most): The organisation says so itself: its press release, website, annual report or a named executive on the record.
  • Regulatory or securities filing (high confidence at most): A filing by the customer or the vendor names the relationship.
  • Independent press (high confidence at most): Editorially independent reporting describes the deployment.
  • Joint announcement (medium confidence at most): A press release issued with the vendor, usually with a quote from the customer.
  • Vendor case study (medium confidence at most): The vendor's published customer story naming the organisation.
  • Vendor mention only (low confidence at most): A logo, a customer list or a passing mention by the vendor, with nothing from the customer.
  • An organisation that also holds a stake in the vendor is labelled “Investor and customer” and is never rated above medium.
  • A partnership is listed as a partner, not a customer.

Questions to ask the vendor (6)

  1. In what year was Gravitational Inc. (Teleport) founded?
    Company age is an input to maturity.
  2. How many full-time employees does Teleport have, and how many work in engineering and customer support?
    Headcount indicates capacity to support a large bank deployment.
  3. Has Teleport reduced headcount since 2022, and by how much?
    Layoffs at a venture-backed vendor can reduce support and product capacity.
  4. Is there any pending or recently concluded material litigation involving Gravitational Inc. (Teleport)?
    Material litigation can affect a supplier's standing and focus.
  5. Have any large customers ended their use of Teleport in the last 24 months, and why?
    Loss of large customers can signal product or service problems.
  6. Have there been any departures or disputes involving Teleport's founders or senior leadership in the last 24 months?
    Leadership stability matters for a founder-led vendor.

Timeline

  1. 2026-11-19 · partnership Teleport
    Teleport gains AWS Security Competency status for identity and access management

    Teleport announced on 2026-11-19 that it has earned AWS Security Competency status in the Identity and Access Management category, an Amazon Web Services partner designation. This is a partner-programme recognition announced by the vendor, not an independent security certification. Teleport (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-22, opens in new tab)

  2. 2026-11-10 · launch Teleport
    Teleport makes Beams, its runtime for AI agents in production infrastructure, generally available

    Teleport announced in a press release dated 2026-11-10 that Beams, in public beta since March 2026, became generally available on 2026-11-09. According to Teleport, Beams runs AI agents in isolated micro-VMs with no standing privileges, reviewed access requests, secretless connections to infrastructure, session monitoring and a kill switch, and is built on its Infrastructure Identity Platform. The release does not state pricing. Teleport (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-22, opens in new tab)

  3. 2026-11-09 · security incident Teleport
    Teleport discloses exposure of internal chat transcripts through sub-processor Notion

    Disclosed by Teleport on 2026-11-11: its sub-processor Notion told it on 9 November 2026 of a data breach affecting Teleport's chat transcripts in the Notion AI app. Teleport said the breach did not occur through its own systems or involve its products, that the transcripts contained links to internal pages and one office guest Wi-Fi password, which it rotated, and no credentials or specific customer data. It notified customers mentioned in the transcripts on 10 November, disabled Notion's AI features and rated the risk to customers as low. Teleport (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  4. 2025-06-20 · vulnerability disclosure Teleport
    Teleport patches critical remote authentication bypass (CVE-2025-49825)

    Reported by SecurityWeek on 2025-06-23: Teleport warned of a critical flaw (CVSS 9.8) allowing remote bypass of SSH authentication, fixed in versions 17.5.2 and earlier maintenance lines. Cloud customers were patched automatically, self-hosted agents had to be updated, and no exploitation in the wild was known. Teleport's trust centre lists a root-cause analysis and indicator-of-compromise instructions for the flaw.
